# artifacts

This directory holds durable evidence bundles that are useful for future maintenance but are not source code, runtime state, or live issue-tracker data.

## 中文说明

Artifacts 是 Claude Code 的能力扩展，用来处理对应领域里的文件、网页、数据或自动化流程。

## 典型场景
- 使用 Artifacts 完成相关任务
- 减少手工复制、整理和重复操作
- 把固定流程交给 Claude Code 执行

# Preserved Project Artifacts

This directory holds durable evidence bundles that are useful for future
maintenance but are not source code, runtime state, or live issue-tracker data.

- `migration-baseline/` contains the frankensearch/FAD migration baseline used
  by `scripts/migration_e2e_validate.sh`.
- `ftui-parity/` contains reviewed FTUI visual-parity audit evidence, baseline
  bundle notes, and the machine-readable parity manifest. The active scoring
  rubric remains in `docs/ftui_visual_parity_rubric.md` because it is a living
  reference, not a captured run artifact.
- `no-mock-audit.md` is the durable audit narrative for the no-mock CI policy;
  the machine-enforced allowlist lives in `tests/policies/`.
- `refactor-runs/` contains preserved simplification/refactor proof bundles
  from prior skill-loop passes.

Archived proof cards may mention their original capture paths, such as
`refactor/artifacts/...`, because those command transcripts are preserved as
historical evidence. For current references, use the paths under this directory.

Transient local logs, ad-hoc command output, temporary databases, and generated
test results should stay ignored. In particular, `tests/artifacts/` is for
local test/profiling output; move only reviewed, durable evidence here when it
has long-term maintenance value.

# FTUI Parity Baseline Bundle (Track A / Bead `2dccg.1.2`)

Status: in progress  
Owner: `BronzeCove`  
Primary manifest: `test-results/visual-parity/2026-02-08/manifest.json`

## Objective
Create a canonical, reproducible evidence bundle comparing ratatui `v0.1.64` and current FTUI, then map deficits to concrete remediation tracks/files so no major baseline failure is unowned.

## Artifacts Produced (Revision 1)
Bundle directory:
- `test-results/visual-parity/2026-02-08`

Baseline (ratatui-era captures):
- `test-results/visual-parity/2026-02-08/baseline-ratatui/search_results_main.webp`
- `test-results/visual-parity/2026-02-08/baseline-ratatui/detail_view.webp`
- `test-results/visual-parity/2026-02-08/baseline-ratatui/help_view.webp`

Candidate (current FTUI captures):
- `test-results/visual-parity/2026-02-08/current-ftui/cassapp_results_wide.snap`
- `test-results/visual-parity/2026-02-08/current-ftui/cassapp_results_narrow.snap`
- `test-results/visual-parity/2026-02-08/current-ftui/pty_search_detail_output.raw`
- `test-results/visual-parity/2026-02-08/current-ftui/pty_search_detail_summary.json`

## Deterministic Context
- Candidate commit: `226ef1d1a01bdfa5183a4c70b4003c189ce90560`
- Candidate version string: `cass 0.1.64`
- Example evidence commands:
  - `cargo test --test e2e_tui_smoke_flows tui_pty_search_detail_and_quit_flow -- --nocapture`
  - `cargo test style_token -- --nocapture`

## Canonical Scenario Matrix (Contract vs Current Coverage)
| Scenario | Contract | Coverage in Rev 1 | Artifact Pair |
|---|---|---|---|
| Search results | required | captured | `search_results_main.webp` vs `cassapp_results_wide.snap` |
| Detail/messages tab | required | captured | `detail_view.webp` vs `pty_search_detail_output.raw` |
| Detail/snippets tab | required | pending | missing pair |
| Detail/json tab | required | pending | missing pair |
| Detail/find-open | required | pending | missing pair |

Why partial coverage is still useful now:
- It already provides deterministic evidence for the highest-frequency surfaces (search + messages detail).
- It unblocks root-cause ownership mapping so implementation tracks can proceed without ambiguity.
- Remaining scenario captures are explicitly enumerated and can be added as follow-up in the same bundle format.

## Root-Cause to Workstream Mapping (Owner Map)
This section is authoritative for “what failure maps to what track/code”.

| Failure Signal | Primary File/Surface | Owning Track(s) | Verification Path |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pills/tabs/keyboard legend looked flat/unwired | `src/ui/app.rs`, `src/ui/style_system.rs` token wiring | Track B (`2dccg.2`) | snapshot + unit invariants (`2dccg.6.2`, `2dccg.11.1`) |
| Markdown theme mismatch against selected preset | `src/ui/app.rs` detail markdown renderer path | Track C (`2dccg.3`) | theme regression tests (`2dccg.3.3`) + E2E (`2dccg.11.3`) |
| Detail find bar weak discoverability | `src/ui/app.rs` detail find render path | Track D (`2dccg.4`) | find state tests (`2dccg.4.3`) + snapshot coverage (`2dccg.6.2`) |
| Over-aggressive degradation flattening | degradation policy + capability logic in UI runtime | Track E (`2dccg.5`) | degradation matrix tests (`2dccg.5.3`, `2dccg.6.3`) |
| Minimal fixture realism hiding regressions | test fixture/snapshot surface | Track F (`2dccg.6`) | fixture + snapshot expansion (`2dccg.6.1`, `2dccg.6.2`) |
| Search-surface context/hierarchy loss | search bar/pills/breadcrumbs/footer HUD | Track H (`2dccg.8`) | search regression suite (`2dccg.8.6`) |
| Results-pane scanability/motion/density regressions | results list/snippets/score cues/animations | Track I (`2dccg.9`) | results regression suite (`2dccg.9.5`) |
| Theme/env/capability inconsistency | style-system semantics, env flags, adaptive policies | Track J (`2dccg.10`) | capability diagnostics (`2dccg.10.9`) |
| End-to-end confidence + triage quality | unit/E2E/logging/CI artifacts | Track K (`2dccg.11`) | full verification bundle (`2dccg.11.8`) |

## Coupling Risks (Explicit)
1. Markdown theme coherence and degradation policy are coupled; one can hide or amplify the other.
2. Search/results visual improvements can mask style-token drift unless token-audit tests stay green.
3. Snapshot-only coverage is insufficient without E2E logging context for failure triage.

## Tradeoffs Taken in Rev 1
1. Prioritized deterministic and reproducible captures over broad one-off screenshot collection.
2. Published a partial scenario matrix now to unblock ownership, while explicitly tracking missing captures.
3. Used existing ratatui-era screenshot assets for baseline continuity in this first bundle revision.

## Remaining Work to Fully Complete `2dccg.1.2`
1. Capture snippets-tab side-by-side artifact pair.
2. Capture json-tab side-by-side artifact pair.
3. Capture find-open side-by-side artifact pair.
4. Add Light + HighContrast variants for the scenario set in the same manifest schema.
5. Add final scored deltas using the rubric in `docs/ftui_visual_parity_rubric.md`.

## How Future Agents Should Extend This Bundle
1. Add files under `test-results/visual-parity/<date>/...`.
2. Append scenario entries in `manifest.json` with explicit `status`.
3. Keep scenario IDs stable; do not rename previously published IDs.
4. Update this document’s matrix and residual-work section in the same commit.

# ftui/ftui-extras Feature Audit for cass

Bead: `coding_agent_session_search-3nwtd.2.1`  
Date: 2026-02-13  
Owner: `GreenMountain`

## Scope and method

This audit compares:

1. What is available in pinned FrankenTUI (`ftui` + `ftui-extras`) at commit `f0ad8a6d9b016ce6a000dc5e1461e1411aee1441`.
2. What cass currently uses in `src/ui/*` and related UI paths.
3. Which high-value capabilities are currently unused.

Primary evidence:

- `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` (pinned rev + enabled features)
- `crates/ftui-extras/src/*` and `crates/ftui-widgets/src/lib.rs` in the pinned checkout
- cass usage scans in `src/ui/app.rs`, `src/ui/analytics_charts.rs`, `src/ui/style_system.rs`

## Version and enabled features

From `Cargo.toml`, cass enables `ftui-extras` features:

- `markdown`, `syntax`, `charts`, `canvas`, `theme`, `clipboard`, `clipboard-fallback`, `export`, `visual-fx`, `forms`, `validation`, `help`

Pinned to:

- `ftui` `0.1.1` at `f0ad8a6d9b016ce6a000dc5e1461e1411aee1441`
- `ftui-extras` `0.1.1` at same rev

## Capability inventory vs current usage

### ftui-extras feature modules

| Feature | Key public capabilities | cass usage now | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `charts` | `Sparkline`, `BarChart`, `LineChart`, `heatmap_gradient` | Used heavily in analytics | `src/ui/analytics_charts.rs:17`, `src/ui/analytics_charts.rs:19` |
| `canvas` | `Painter` + `CanvasRef`, modes (`Braille`, `Block`, `HalfBlock`), primitives (`point`, `line`, `rect`, `rect_filled`, `polygon_filled`, `circle`) | Used narrowly for heatmap raster fill | `src/ui/analytics_charts.rs:16`, `src/ui/analytics_charts.rs:1069` |
| `markdown` | `MarkdownRenderer`, `MarkdownTheme`, markdown detection helpers | Used in detail modal rendering | `src/ui/app.rs:141`, `src/ui/style_system.rs:25` |
| `clipboard` | `Clipboard::auto`, selections/backends | Used for copy actions | `src/ui/app.rs:15560` |
| `export` | `HtmlExporter`, `SvgExporter`, `TextExporter` | Used for screenshot export path | `src/ui/app.rs:14565` |
| `visual-fx` | `FxQuality`, `Backdrop`, `Scrim`, `FxLayer`, `StackedFx`, effects (`MetaballsFx`, `PlasmaFx`), canvas adapters | Not used | no `ftui_extras::visual_fx` usage in `src/` |
| `forms` | `Form`, `FormField`, `FormState`, `ConfirmDialog` | Not used | no `ftui_extras::forms` usage in `src/` |
| `validation` | composable validators (`Required`, `MinLength`, `Email`, `ValidatorBuilder`) + async/deadline coordinators | Not used | no `ftui_extras::validation` usage in `src/` |
| `help` | `Tooltip`, `Spotlight`, guided `Tour` state | Not used | no `ftui_extras::help` usage in `src/` |
| `theme` | theme registry + semantic token helpers | Not used directly (cass uses its own style system) | no `ftui_extras::theme` usage in `src/` |
| `syntax` | language tokenizers/highlighter APIs | Not used directly | no `ftui_extras::syntax` usage in `src/` |

### Chart/canvas/FX detail inventory (requested deep scope)

#### Charts (available)

- Chart types: `Sparkline`, `BarChart`, `LineChart`.
- Useful builder knobs currently available:
  - `Sparkline`: `style`, `min`, `max`, `gradient`
  - `BarChart`: direction (`Vertical`/`Horizontal`), mode (`Grouped`/`Stacked`), `bar_width`, `bar_gap`, `group_gap`, `colors`, bounds
  - `LineChart`: bounds, labels, legend toggle, per-series markers

Current cass usage:

- Uses all three chart types, but in static render mode.
- No chart widget-level hit test plumbing for direct click-to-drill; drilldown is list-row based.

#### Canvas (available)

- Modes: `Braille` (2x4), `Block` (2x2), `HalfBlock` (1x2).
- Primitives: point, colored point, line, colored line, rect, filled rect, filled polygon, circle, metaball field rendering helper.

Current cass usage:

- Uses `Painter::for_area` + `point_colored` loops for heatmap block fills.
- Does not use line/circle/polygon/metaball primitives yet.

#### Visual FX (available)

- Core: `FxQuality`, `ThemeInputs`, `BackdropFx`, `FxLayer`, `StackedFx`, scrim blending and quality clamping.
- Exported effects: `MetaballsFx`, `PlasmaFx`, samplers, optional canvas adapters.
- Infrastructure supports graceful degradation alignment with frame budget.

Current cass usage:

- No active usage in app rendering pipeline.
- Existing app has its own stagger reveal hooks but no `ftui_extras::visual_fx` backdrop composition.

## ftui widgets surface: available vs used

`ftui-widgets` exposes 57 widget modules at this pinned rev.  
cass directly imports a small subset in production UI:

- `block`, `borders`, `command_palette`, `help_registry`, `hint_ranker`, `json_view`, `paragraph`, `focus`, `virtualized`, `inspector`

Observation:

- cass already uses advanced core widgets (command palette, hint ranker, virtualized list, inspector).
- There is still unused headroom in core widgets (`table`, `progress`, `spinner`, `modal`, `toast`, etc.) that could simplify some custom rendering logic.

## Prioritized gap analysis

### High value gaps

1. No direct chart interaction bridge (click/select point -> filtered search drilldown)
- Impact: blocks a key goal in Feature B/C.
- Best follow-up: `3nwtd.2.2`, then `3nwtd.3.2`.

2. Canvas is underused for analytics beyond heatmap fill
- Missing: scatter/area/shape-based renderings despite primitive support.
- Best follow-up: `3nwtd.2.4`.

3. `visual-fx` not integrated into surface transitions/loading polish
- Missing: backdrop/scrim-based motion and composited transitions.
- Best follow-up: `3nwtd.4.1`, `3nwtd.4.2`.

### Medium value gaps

1. `syntax` feature is enabled but not directly exercised by cass UI code
- Markdown is rendered, but there is no explicit syntax highlighter integration path in cass-owned code.

2. `help` tours/tooltips are unused
- Could improve onboarding and discoverability of dense keyboard workflows.

3. `forms` + `validation` are unused
- Could standardize interactive config/filter dialogs and reduce hand-rolled validation logic.

### Low value / opportunistic gaps

1. `ftui_extras::theme` is unused directly
- cass has robust custom style system already; migration benefit is incremental, not urgent.

2. Export path could evolve from snapshot-only to richer share/report bundles
- APIs already present (`HtmlExporter`, `SvgExporter`, `TextExporter`) and partially used.

## Recommended execution sequence

1. Land this audit (current bead).
2. Implement interactive chart drilldown (`3nwtd.2.2`) with explicit selection model and query handoff contract.
3. Add one canvas-native analytics panel (`3nwtd.2.4`) as a proof point (scatter + area fill).
4. Integrate `visual-fx` backdrop transitions gated by degradation (`3nwtd.4.1`).
5. Add loading states tied to async boundaries (`3nwtd.4.2`), using spinner/progress where practical.

## Practical implementation notes for next beads

- Keep `analytics_charts.rs` as the chart orchestration layer; route all drilldown intents through typed `CassMsg` events.
- Reuse existing `selection` plumbing already present in analytics views before adding new input modes.
- Wire any visual FX through quality gates (`FxQuality::from_degradation_with_area`) to preserve frame budget guarantees.
- Prefer incremental view-level activation flags so new visuals can be A/B tested without destabilizing all analytics views at once.

    let total_slots = self.config.read().await.total_slots;  // Line 116
    let mut current = self.used_slots.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
    loop {

        }
        match self.used_slots.compare_exchange(
            current,
            current + count,
            Ordering::SeqCst,
            Ordering::Relaxed,

            Err(actual) => current = actual,

```

**Bug Scenario:** Between line 116 (reading `total_slots`) and the loop starting, another task could modify `total_slots` via `update_config()`. ## **RECOMMENDATIONS**

1. **Store JoinHandles:** Keep references to spawned task handles and propagate panics to the main task or at least log them properly.

2. **Minimize Lock Duration:** Release locks immediately after acquiring the data needed. Refactor the health monitor to avoid holding write locks across multiple awaits.

3. **Atomic Consistency:** Make slot reservation atomic at the logical level by holding the config read lock or using compare-and-swap with consistent memory ordering.

4. **Timeout Network Operations:** Wrap SSH operations in `tokio::time::timeout()` to enforce the configured timeout.

5. **Backpressure on Queues:** Implement maximum queue depth with proper rejection handling.

6. **Drain State Transitions:** Use a single atomic state machine (e.g., `AtomicU8` with variants) to ensure drain transitions are atomic with slot checks.

7. **Memory Ordering Consistency:** Use `SeqCst` ordering or carefully justify `Relaxed` loads with synchronization-point documentation.

8. **Error Propagation:** Catch panics in spawned tasks using `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` with result handling, or use a global panic hook.

### 1. **CRITICAL: TCP Connection Leak in SFTP Sync (src/sources/sync.rs:657-675)**

**Location**: Lines 657, 675, 678-680

**Issue**: Asymmetric resource lifecycle for TCP stream clones

**Root Cause**:
- Line 657: `tcp_shutdown = tcp.try_clone().ok()` creates an optional clone of the TCP stream
- Line 675: The original `tcp` is moved into `session.set_tcp_stream(tcp)` 
- Lines 678-680: The closure only shuts down `tcp_shutdown` (if it exists), never the TCP stream that was passed to `session.set_tcp_stream()`

**Problem**: When the SSH session owns the primary TCP stream but only the secondary clone is explicitly shut down, there's potential for:
- Double-shutdown attempts (the session may try to shut down, then the closure tries to shut down the clone)
- Resource leak if the primary stream doesn't get properly closed by the session on early errors
- Shutdown ordering issues: line 663 tries to shutdown `tcp` before it's moved to the session, but after Session::new() fails, the `tcp` is still held by this function and doesn't get moved

**Specific Problem Case at Line 663**:
When `Session::new()` fails:
```rust
let mut session = match Session::new() {
    Ok(s) => s,
    Err(e) => {
        let _ = tcp.shutdown(Shutdown::Both);  // Line 663 - shuts down original
        return PathSyncResult { ... };          // Returns without issue here
    }
};
```
This path is actually safe. However, the design is fragile because:
1. Only the clone (`tcp_shutdown`) gets shut down in `close_connections`
2. The original `tcp` handed to `session.set_tcp_stream()` relies entirely on session cleanup
3. If session cleanup fails silently, the original stream may not be properly closed

**Recommendation**: Pass the same stream handle to the closure instead of relying on the clone pattern.

**Location**: Lines 305-313

**Issue**: Unbounded memory allocation from network input

**Root Cause**:
```rust
let len = u32::from_be_bytes(len_buf) as usize;
if len > 100 * 1024 * 1024 {  // Line 306 - 100MB limit check
    warn!(len = len, "Request too large, closing connection");
    return Ok(());
}

// Read request payload
let mut payload = vec![0u8; len];  // Line 312 - allocates without further validation
stream.read_exact(&mut payload)?;
```

**Problem**:
- A malicious client can send a length prefix of exactly 100MB (or just under)
- Line 312 will allocate 100MB of heap memory in a single vector
- With default max_connections=16, an attacker could allocate up to 1.6GB of RAM
- No rate limiting or connection-level quotas
- This happens on the main thread before any actual message validation

**Impact**: Denial of Service - memory exhaustion attack on the daemon

**Recommendation**: 
- Reduce the buffer limit or implement streaming deserialization
- Add per-connection memory tracking
- Implement rate limiting on connection count or message frequency

```rust
// List directory contents
let entries = sftp
    .readdir(remote_path)
    .map_err(|e| format!("Failed to list {}: {}", remote_path.display(), e))?;

for (entry_path, entry_stat) in entries {

            &sftp,
            &entry_path,
            &local_entry,
            files_transferred,
            &mut bytes_transferred,
        )?;  // Line 880 - early return propagates error
    }
}
```

**Problem**:
- If recursion fails partway through the loop at line 880, the function returns immediately
- Any SFTP file handles opened in the current directory iteration may not be properly closed
- The `readdir()` iterator may hold internal resources that aren't cleaned up
- Subsequent retries or cleanup operations might fail due to lingering handles

**Impact**: Resource leaks during partial SFTP sync failures, especially with deep directory trees

**Recommendation**: 
- Consider wrapping the directory iteration in explicit cleanup
- Or implement a breadth-first traversal with explicit error recovery per-entry
- Add explicit close/cleanup calls before returning errors

### 4. **Unchecked Error Path in SSH Authentication (src/sources/sync.rs:785-795)**

**Location**: Lines 785-795

**Issue**: Silent fallback when SSH agent fails

if let Ok(mut agent) = session.agent()

    && agent.list_identities().is_ok()

        }

**Problem**:
- Line 789: `agent.identities()` is called after `list_identities()` succeeded, but there's no guarantee the identity list is still valid
- If `agent.identities()` returns `Err`, it silently becomes an empty default list

**Impact**: Authentication debugging complexity, silent failures in agent path

### 5. **Memory Overflow in Daemon Connection Limit Check (src/daemon/core.rs:240-242)**

**Location**: Lines 240-242

**Issue**: Off-by-one in connection limit enforcement

let active = self.active_connections.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
if active >= self.config.max_connections as u64 {

**Problem**:

- If `active == max_connections - 1` before the add, it will be `max_connections` after

### 10. **Ordered Atomic Relaxed Loads Without Synchronization (Workers.rs)**

**File: `/data/projects/remote_compilation_helper/rchd/src/workers.rs` lines 109-112, 382-383**

**Issue:** The `available_slots()` method loads `used_slots` atomically with Relaxed ordering, then reads `total_slots` via RwLock:

pub async fn available_slots(&self) -> u32 {

**Impact:** Inconsistent slot availability readings in worker selection, potentially allowing overallocation.

1. **Store JoinHandles:** Keep references to spawned task handles and propagate panics to the main task or at least log them properly.

3. **Atomic Consistency:** Make slot reservation atomic at the logical level by holding the config read lock or using compare-and-swap with consistent memory ordering.

4. **Timeout Network Operations:** Wrap SSH operations in `tokio::time::timeout()` to enforce the configured timeout.

5. **Backpressure on Queues:** Implement maximum queue depth with proper rejection handling.

6. **Drain State Transitions:** Use a single atomic state machine (e.g., `AtomicU8` with variants) to ensure drain transitions are atomic with slot checks.

7. **Memory Ordering Consistency:** Use `SeqCst` ordering or carefully justify `Relaxed` loads with synchronization-point documentation.

8. **Error Propagation:** Catch panics in spawned tasks using `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` with result handling, or use a global panic hook.

### Executive Summary

The **Flywheel Connector Protocol (FCP) V2** is a sophisticated, mesh-native security framework for distributed AI agent operations across personal device networks. It replaces the hub-spoke model with cryptographic isolation, capability-based access control, and symbol-addressed data distribution. **Key Innovation**: Instead of central coordination, FCP uses three foundational axioms: Universal Fungibility (RaptorQ fountain codes), Authenticated Mesh (Tailscale identity), and Explicit Authority (cryptographic capabilities).

## 4. SDK Pattern for Connector Development

### Minimal Connector Template (from tests)

```rust
#[derive(Debug)]
struct MinimalConnector {
    base: BaseConnector,
}

#[async_trait]
impl FcpConnector for MinimalConnector {
    fn id(&self) -> &ConnectorId {
        &self.base.id
    }

    async fn configure(&mut self, _config: serde_json::Value) -> FcpResult<()> {
        self.base.set_configured(true);
        Ok(())
    }

    async fn handshake(&mut self, req: HandshakeRequest) -> FcpResult<HandshakeResponse> {
        self.base.set_handshaken(true);
        Ok(HandshakeResponse {
            status: "accepted".to_string(),
            capabilities_granted: vec![],
            session_id: SessionId::new(),
            manifest_hash: "sha256:...".to_string(),
            nonce: req.nonce,
            event_caps: None,
            auth_caps: None,
            op_catalog_hash: None,
        })
    }

    async fn health(&self) -> HealthSnapshot {
        HealthSnapshot::ready()
    }

    fn metrics(&self) -> ConnectorMetrics {
        self.base.metrics()
    }

    async fn shutdown(&mut self, _req: ShutdownRequest) -> FcpResult<()> {
        Ok(())
    }

    fn introspect(&self) -> Introspection {
        Introspection {
            connector_id: self.base.id.clone(),
            version: "1.0.0".to_string(),
            archetypes: vec!["request-response".to_string()],
            operations: vec![],
            capabilities: vec![],
        }
    }

    async fn invoke(&self, _req: InvokeRequest) -> FcpResult<InvokeResponse> {
        Ok(InvokeResponse::success("result".into()))
    }

    async fn subscribe(&self, _req: SubscribeRequest) -> FcpResult<SubscribeResponse> {
        let (tx, rx) = broadcast::channel(1000);
        Ok(SubscribeResponse {
            subscription_id: SubscriptionId::new(),
            capabilities: EventCaps::default(),
            requires_ack: false,
            stream: Box::pin(BroadcastStream::new(rx).map(|msg| Ok(msg))),
        })
    }
}
```

### Connector Lifecycle (State Machine)

1. **Instantiation**: `new()` creates BaseConnector with ConnectorId
2. **Configuration**: `configure(config)` → sets `configured = true`
3. **Handshake**: `handshake(req)` → validates client, sets `handshaken = true`, negotiates capabilities
4. **Ready**: `check_ready()` succeeds when both flags true
5. **Operations**: `invoke()`, `subscribe()`, `simulate()` etc. available
6. **Graceful Shutdown**: `shutdown(req)` → drains pending, releases resources

### Architecture Patterns Used

- **Async-Trait**: All trait methods are async-compatible (Tokio runtime)
- **Broadcast Channels**: Event streaming with multiple subscribers
- **Error Taxonomy**: Structured error types with recovery hints
- **Metrics Atomicity**: Lock-free metrics via `AtomicU64`
- **Type Safety**: Canonical IDs prevent typos and data corruption

## 7. Implementation Patterns & Best Practices

### Error Handling Taxonomy

```
FcpError categories (all serializable):
├── FCP-1xxx: Protocol errors (InvalidRequest, MalformedFrame, VersionMismatch)
├── FCP-2xxx: Auth errors (Unauthorized, TokenExpired, InvalidSignature)
├── FCP-3xxx: Capability errors (CapabilityDenied, RateLimited, OperationNotGranted)
├── FCP-4xxx: Zone errors (ZoneViolation, TaintViolation, ElevationRequired)
├── FCP-5xxx: Connector errors (ConnectorUnavailable, NotReady, NotConfigured)
├── FCP-6xxx: Resource errors (ResourceExhausted, StorageQuotaExceeded)
├── FCP-7xxx: External service errors (RemoteServiceError, NetworkTimeout)
└── FCP-9xxx: Internal errors (InternalFailure, ImplementationBug)

Each error includes:
- Human-readable message
- Machine-readable code
- Serializable to JSON for wire protocol
- Recovery hints (e.g., retry_after_ms for rate limits)
```

### Idempotency & Exactly-Once Semantics

**Pattern**: Use idempotency keys for retry safety
```rust
pub struct InvokeRequest {
    pub idempotency_key: Option<String>,
    // ...
}

pub struct OperationIntent {
    pub idempotency_key: Option<String>,
    pub request_object_id: ObjectId,
    pub capability_token_jti: Uuid,
    pub planned_at: u64,
    // ...
}

pub struct OperationReceipt {
    pub intent: ObjectId,
    pub result: Value,
    pub completed_at: u64,
    // ...
}
```

**Implementation**:
1. Create `OperationIntent` BEFORE side effects
2. Store intent in persistent store
3. Execute operation
4. Create `OperationReceipt` AFTER execution
5. On retry with same key → return cached receipt (no re-execution)

### Streaming & Event Management

**Pattern**: Broadcast channel + async stream
```rust
pub struct MyConnector {
    event_tx: broadcast::Sender<FcpResult<EventEnvelope>>,
}

#[async_trait]
impl FcpConnector for MyConnector {
    async fn subscribe(&self, req: SubscribeRequest) -> FcpResult<SubscribeResponse> {
        let rx = self.event_tx.subscribe();
        let stream = Box::pin(BroadcastStream::new(rx).map(|msg| {
            msg.map_err(|_| FcpError::ConnectorUnavailable {
                code: 5001,
                message: "Subscription closed".into(),
            })
        }));
        
        Ok(SubscribeResponse {
            subscription_id: SubscriptionId::new(),
            event_stream: stream,
            capabilities: EventCaps { requires_ack: true, ..Default::default() },
        })
    }
}

// In background task:
async fn run_events(tx: broadcast::Sender<FcpResult<EventEnvelope>>) {
    loop {
        let event = fetch_event().await;
        let envelope = EventEnvelope::new("event.type", EventData::Json(event));
        let _ = tx.send(Ok(envelope)); // Broadcast to all subscribers
    }
}
```

#[async_trait]
impl FcpConnector for MyConnector {
    async fn health(&self) -> HealthSnapshot {
        match self.client_is_healthy() {

}

### Simulation (Preflight Check) Pattern

```rust
#[async_trait]
impl FcpConnector for MyConnector {
    async fn simulate(&self, req: SimulateRequest) -> FcpResult<SimulateResponse> {
        // Check capability
        self.verify_capability(&req.capability_token)?;
        
        // Check resource availability
        let available = self.estimate_availability(&req.operation_id).await?;
        
        // Estimate cost
        let cost = match req.operation_id.as_str() {
            "send_message" => CostEstimate {
                cost: Some(CurrencyCost { amount: 0.01, currency: "USD".into() }),
                ..Default::default()
            },
            _ => CostEstimate::default(),
        };
        
        Ok(SimulateResponse {
            id: req.id,
            allowed: available,
            reason: if available { None } else { Some("Quota exceeded".into()) },
            cost: Some(cost),
            availability: Some(available),
        })
    }
}
```

## 9. Key Innovations & Design Decisions

### 1. **Universal Fungibility via RaptorQ**
- Objects distributed as interchangeable symbols
- Any K' symbols reconstruct the original
- Enables offline-first and multipath resilience

### 2. **Capability Tokens as COSE/CWT**
- Cryptographically signed authority proofs
- Can be delegated and composed
- Serializable and verifiable offline

### 3. **Zone-Based Isolation**
- Cryptographic namespaces (not just policy)
- Encryption keys per zone
- Tailscale ACL + crypto enforcement

### 4. **Exactly-Once Semantics via Intents**
- `OperationIntent` stored BEFORE side effects
- `OperationReceipt` created AFTER
- Idempotency keys prevent re-execution on retry

### 5. **Provenance & Taint Tracking**
- Information flow policy (lattice-based)
- Integrity and confidentiality labels
- Taint accumulation and sanitization receipts

### 6. **Quorum-Signed Objects**
- Byzantine-fault-tolerant consensus
- Configurable thresholds (safe/risky/dangerous/critical)
- Deterministic signature ordering

### 7. **Secretless Credential Injection**
- Connectors reference `CredentialId`, not raw secrets
- Egress proxy injects credentials at network boundary
- Audit trail for credential usage

### 8. **Mesh-Native Architecture**
- Every device is a potential Hub
- No central coordinator required
- Symbol distribution via gossip

Based on my thorough exploration of the codebase, here's the complete picture of how skills are uploaded in this project:

### 1. CLI COMMAND FOR PUSHING/UPLOADING SKILLS

**Command:** `jsm push`

**Location:** `/data/projects/jeffreys-skills.md/cli/src/commands/push.rs`

**Usage:**
```bash
jsm push <path> [--message "changelog message"] [--lint-changelog]
```

**Key Details:**
- Takes a skill directory path as input
- Optional `--message` flag for changelog entry
- Optional `--lint-changelog` flag to validate changelog format before pushing
- Fully async operation using Tokio

**The Push Workflow (from push.rs):**

1. **Validate** the skill directory structure using `validate_skill_directory()`
2. **Lint changelog** (if requested) using `lint_changelog()`
3. **Create ZIP archive** of the skill using `create_zip_archive()`
4. **Compute content hash** - SHA-256 of the skill content for versioning
5. **Read SKILL.md** for server-side content validation
6. **Authenticate** using either:
   - X-API-Key header (for API key auth)
   - Authorization Bearer token (for OAuth)
7. **Send metadata** to `/api/skills/push` endpoint as JSON with PushRequest structure
8. **Receive upload URL** (pre-signed Supabase URL)
9. **Upload ZIP** to signed URL with PUT request and `Content-Type: application/zip` header

**PushRequest Structure:**
```rust
struct PushRequest {
    name: String,
    description: Option<String>,
    category: Option<String>,
    tags: Vec<String>,
    content_hash: String,
    changelog: Option<String>,
    skill_md_content: Option<String>,  // REQUIRED for security
}
```

**Location:** `/data/projects/jeffreys-skills.md/src/app/api/admin/skills/push/route.ts`

#### `/api/skills/push` Workflow:

1. **Rate limiting** enforced before auth
2. **User authentication** required (OAuth or API key)
3. **Account status check** - rejects if user is suspended
4. **Captcha verification** (Turnstile) if enabled
5. **Input validation:**
   - Required fields: `name`, `content_hash`
   - Required for security: `skill_md_content` (prevents bypassing content checks)
   - Valid content_hash format: 64-char hex string (SHA-256)
6. **Content validation:**
   - Protected skill names (cannot use reserved/prefixed names)
   - Protected content check (prevents certain patterns)
   - Compatibility tags validation
7. **Database transaction:**
   - Find or create skill (owner = current user)
   - Check if version already exists (by content_hash)
   - If exists, return `status: "exists"` with version number
   - If new: generate next version number
   - Create storage path: `{userId}/{skillId}/v{versionNumber}_{contentHash}.zip`
   - Generate signed upload URL via Supabase
   - Create skillVersions record
   - Update current version pointer

**Response Format:**
```json

  "skill_id": "uuid",
  "version": 1,
  "upload_url": "https://...",  // Supabase signed URL
  "token": "...",

}

5. **Download mechanism:**

**Location:** `/data/projects/jeffreys-skills.md/src/lib/db/schema.ts` (lines 253-274)

**Table Definition:**
```typescript
export const skillVersions = pgTable(
  "skill_versions",
  {
    id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
    skillId: uuid("skill_id")
      .references(() => skills.id, { onDelete: "cascade" })
      .notNull(),
    versionNumber: integer("version_number").notNull(),
    contentHash: text("content_hash").notNull(),        // SHA-256 of normalized zip
    skillHash: text("skill_hash"),                      // Canonical hash with sha256: prefix
    storagePath: text("storage_path").notNull(),        // Supabase Storage path
    changelog: text("changelog"),                       // Version changelog/release notes
    createdAt: timestamp("created_at", { withTimezone: true }).defaultNow().notNull(),
    removedAt: timestamp("removed_at", { withTimezone: true }),  // Soft delete (null = active)
    removalReason: text("removal_reason"),              // Admin-provided moderation reason
  },
  (table) => [
    uniqueIndex("skill_versions_skill_version_idx").on(table.skillId, table.versionNumber),
    index("skill_versions_hash_idx").on(table.contentHash),
    uniqueIndex("skill_versions_skill_hash_idx").on(table.skillHash),
  ]
);
```

**Key Fields Explained:**

| Field | Type | Purpose |
|-------|------|---------|
| `id` | UUID | Primary key, auto-generated |
| `skillId` | UUID FK | References parent skill |
| `versionNumber` | Integer | Auto-incrementing version (1, 2, 3...) |
| `contentHash` | Text | SHA-256 of skill zip - prevents duplicate uploads |
| `skillHash` | Text | Optional canonical hash with `sha256:` prefix |
| `storagePath` | Text | Full Supabase Storage path to zip file |
| `changelog` | Text | User-provided release notes for this version |
| `createdAt` | Timestamp | When version was uploaded |
| `removedAt` | Timestamp | Soft-delete marker for moderation (null = active) |
| `removalReason` | Text | Why version was removed (abuse, DMCA, etc.) |

**Index Strategy:**

1. **Unique (skillId, versionNumber)** - Ensures one version per number per skill
2. **Regular on contentHash** - Fast duplicate detection
3. **Unique on skillHash** - Optional canonical hash lookup

**Related Tables:**

The `skills` table references current version:
```typescript
currentVersionId: uuid("current_version_id"),  // Foreign key to skillVersions.id
```

This allows efficient retrieval of the latest version without scanning all versions.

## 4. Protocol Implementations

### FCPS (Flywheel Connector Protocol - Symbol/Data-Plane)

**Location**: `crates/fcp-protocol/fcps.rs`

**Wire format** (114-byte fixed header + symbols):
- Magic: "FCPS" (4 bytes)
- Version, Flags, Symbol count, Payload length
- Object ID, Symbol size, Zone key ID, Zone ID hash
- Epoch ID, Sender instance ID, Frame sequence
- Per-symbol: ESI (4) + K (2) + data + auth_tag (16)

**Frame flags** (RaptorQ symbol encoding):
- `REQUIRES_ACK`, `COMPRESSED`, `ENCRYPTED`, `RESPONSE`, `ERROR`, `STREAMING`, `STREAM_END`
- `HAS_CAP_TOKEN`, `ZONE_CROSSING`, `PRIORITY`, `RAPTORQ`, `CONTROL_PLANE`

**Default**: `ENCRYPTED | RAPTORQ`

### FCPC (Flywheel Connector Protocol - Control/Control-Plane)

**Location**: `crates/fcp-protocol/fcpc.rs` (Recently added - commit 0537c38)

**Fixed header**: 36 bytes (magic + version + session_id + seq + flags + len)
- Magic: "FCPC"
- Version: 1
- Session ID: 16 bytes (MeshSessionId)
- Sequence: u64 (monotonic per direction)
- Flags: Encrypted (by default), compressed support
- Payload length: u32

**Authenticated with**: Session `k_ctx` (ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD)

**Max payload**: 4 MiB default

### Session Handshake (`fcp-protocol/session.rs`)

**Session constants**:
- `SESSION_ID_SIZE`: 16 bytes
- `SESSION_NONCE_SIZE`: 16 bytes (hello/ack nonces)
- `SESSION_COOKIE_SIZE`: 32 bytes (stateless cookie)
- `SESSION_MAC_SIZE`: 16 bytes (truncated HMAC tag)
- `DEFAULT_MAX_DATAGRAM_BYTES`: 1200 (MTU-safe)

**Crypto suites** (NORMATIVE):
- **Suite1**: X25519 + HKDF-SHA256 + HMAC-SHA256 (tag truncated to 16)
- **Suite2**: X25519 + HKDF-SHA256 + BLAKE3-keyed (tag truncated to 16)

## 8. Key Security Concepts

### Zone Architecture

```
z:owner        [Trust: 100]  ← Most privileged
    ↓
z:private      [Trust: 80]   ← Personal data
    ↓
z:work         [Trust: 60]   ← Professional
    ↓
z:community    [Trust: 40]   ← Trusted external
    ↓
z:public       [Trust: 20]   ← Public/anonymous
```

**Invariants**:
- **Integrity**: Data flows DOWN (higher → lower) freely; UP requires `ApprovalToken`
- **Confidentiality**: Data flows UP (lower → higher) freely; DOWN requires `ApprovalToken` (declassification)

### Core Security Axioms

1. **Universal Fungibility**: All durable mesh objects are symbol-addressable (RaptorQ)
2. **Authenticated Mesh**: Tailscale IS transport AND identity layer
3. **Explicit Authority**: No ambient authority; capabilities flow through cryptographic chains

### Five Cryptographic Key Roles

| Key Type | Algorithm | Purpose |
|----------|-----------|---------|
| **Owner Key** | Ed25519 | Root trust anchor; signs attestations, revocations (SHOULD use FROST threshold) |
| **Node Signing Key** | Ed25519 | Per-device; signs frames, gossip, receipts |
| **Node Encryption Key** | X25519 | Per-device; receives sealed zone keys and secret shares |
| **Node Issuance Key** | Ed25519 | Per-device; mints capability tokens (separately revocable) |
| **Zone Encryption Key** | ChaCha20-Poly1305 | Per-zone symmetric key; encrypts zone data via AEAD |

### Key Architectural Principles

#### 1. Observation vs Action Separation

The system splits runtime into two conceptual loops:

**Observation Loop (Passive)**:
```
Poll Panes → Capture Output → Persist to DB → Detect Patterns → Emit Events
    ↑________________________________________________________________│
                    (never modifies terminal state)
```

**Action Loop (Active)**:
```
Receive Event → Re-check State → Validate Guards → Execute → Verify
    ↑________________________________________________________________│
                (always re-validates before acting)
```

**Critical Invariant**: The action loop never runs on stale assumptions; it always re-checks current pane state before sending any input.

#### 2. Component Responsibilities

| Component | Role | Key Properties |
|-----------|------|-----------------|
| **Ingest Pipeline** | Discover panes, tail output deltas | Per-pane cursors, backpressure, gap events |
| **Event Bus** | Fan-out stream for deltas, detections | Bounded channels, multi-consumer, no blocking |
| **Pattern Engine** | Match output against patterns | SIMD-accelerated, sub-millisecond, state-aware |
| **Workflow Engine** | Execute durable automated responses | Persistent FSM, step logging, resumable |
| **Robot Mode** | Agent-optimized CLI/MCP interface | JSON/Markdown output, token-efficient |
| **Storage Layer** | Persist segments, events, state | SQLite WAL, FTS5 search, async-safe |
| **WezTerm Interface** | Abstract all WezTerm interactions | CLI primary, optional deep integration |

## Architecture Highlights

### Safety by Design

1. **No Unsafe Code**: `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` at workspace level
2. **Type Safety**: Strong error types, zero string-based errors
3. **Guard Checks**: Policy engine validates before actions
4. **Observation-First**: Workflows always re-validate before acting
5. **Rate Limiting**: Per-pane throttling prevents runaway automation
6. **Graceful Degradation**: Failures handled, not propagated

### Performance Considerations

1. **Zero-Copy Patterns**: Leverage SIMD via aho-corasick
2. **Async/Await**: Tokio runtime for non-blocking I/O
3. **Bounded Channels**: Event bus prevents memory explosion
4. **SQLite WAL**: Concurrent read/write access
5. **Compact Binary**: Release profile optimized for size and speed

### Extensibility

1. **Pattern Packs**: Pluggable pattern libraries
2. **Workflow Definition**: Declarative step-based workflows
3. **Agent Support**: Extensible agent type enum
4. **Unknown Field Tolerance**: JSON forward compatibility
5. **MCP Ready**: Scaffolding for external tool integration

### Key Design Decisions

1. **CLI Primary, MCP Optional**: WezTerm CLI is reliable baseline
2. **Per-Pane State Tracking**: Enables precise cursor management
3. **Deterministic Detection**: No timing heuristics
4. **Durable Workflows**: Persist state for recovery
5. **Event-Driven Architecture**: Decoupled components via event bus

## How the Pieces Fit Together

### Data Flow Example: Usage Limit Detection & Recovery

```
1. Ingest Pipeline polls pane output every 200ms
   ↓
2. New output detected: "Usage limit reached: 8M / 8M tokens"
   ↓
3. Output persisted to SQLite segment table
   ↓
4. Pattern engine detects "codex:usage_reached" pattern
   ↓
5. Detection event emitted to event bus
   ↓
6. Workflow engine receives event, validates pane state
   ↓
7. Starts "handle_usage_limits" workflow:
   - Step 1: Send pause signal to agent
   - Step 2: Wait for "paused" confirmation
   - Step 3: Wait for reset time (waits for external signal or timer)
   - Step 4: Send resume signal
   - Step 5: Log completion
   ↓
8. Robot mode client queries events/state for next action
```

### Multi-Agent Coordination Example

```
Controller Agent (Claude Code):
- Polls: wa robot state → get all panes
- Sends:  wa send <pane_id> "what should we do next?"
- Queries: wa robot search "error" → find any errors
- Manages: wa workflow run handle_compaction --pane <id>

Worker Agents (running in panes):
- Execute commands
- Output goes to terminal
- wa daemon captures + detects patterns
- Workflows automatically respond to limits
```

### 1. **How to Enumerate Segments**

The primary methods on `Index` for discovering segments are:

- **`searchable_segments() -> Vec<Segment>`** - Returns the list of segment objects that are currently searchable
- **`searchable_segment_ids() -> Vec<SegmentId>`** - Returns just the segment identifiers for all searchable segments
- **`searchable_segment_metas() -> Vec<SegmentMeta>`** - Reads the `meta.json` file and returns complete segment metadata objects from the last commit
- **`load_metas() -> IndexMeta`** - Reads and returns the entire index meta file containing all segment metadata

### 2. **How Segment IDs Work**

**SegmentId** is a UUID-based wrapper type:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SegmentId(Uuid);
```

**Key Methods on SegmentId:**
- `generate_random() -> SegmentId` - Creates a new random segment identifier
- `short_uuid_string() -> String` - Returns first 8 characters of the UUID (e.g., "a5c4dfcb") for display
- `uuid_string() -> String` - Returns full 32-character lowercase hex UUID
- `from_uuid_string(uuid_str: &str) -> Result<SegmentId, ...>` - Parses a UUID string into SegmentId
- `FromStr` trait implementation for parsing from strings
- Implements `Ord` for sorting and comparison operations

All segment files use the naming convention: `segment_uuid.component_extension` (or `segment_uuid.delete_opstamp.component_extension` for delete files).

### 3. **How to List Component Files for a Segment**

The **SegmentMeta** object provides file enumeration:

- **`list_files() -> HashSet<PathBuf>`** - Returns all files required for the segment as a set of PathBuf objects
- **`relative_path(component: SegmentComponent) -> PathBuf`** - Returns the relative path of a specific component by joining the segment ID with the component's file extension

The **Segment** object offers direct file access:

- **`meta() -> &SegmentMeta`** - Access the segment's metadata
- **`relative_path(component: SegmentComponent) -> PathBuf`** - Get the path for a component
- **`open_read(component: SegmentComponent) -> Result<FileSlice, ...>`** - Opens a component file for reading
- **`open_write(component: SegmentComponent) -> Result<WritePtr, ...>`** - Opens a component file for writing

### 4. **Segment Component Types (SegmentComponent Enum)**

There are 8 distinct file types in each segment:

1. **Postings** - Sorted lists of document IDs associated with terms
2. **Positions** - Positions of terms within each document (for phrase queries)
3. **FastFields** - Column-oriented random-access storage for field values
4. **FieldNorms** - Sum of field term lengths for each document
5. **Terms** - Dictionary mapping Terms to TermInfo (offsets into postings/positions files)
6. **Store** - Row-oriented compressed storage of document fields
7. **TempStore** - Temporary storage before being streamed to Store

### 7. **The SegmentMeta Struct - Complete Interface**

**Identification & Counting:**

- `num_docs() -> u32` - Total documents in segment

### 2. Tokenizer Registration
```rust
pub fn register_tokenizer(index: &Index) {
    let analyzer = TextAnalyzer::builder(SimpleTokenizer::default())
        .filter(LowerCaser)
        .filter(RemoveLongFilter::limit(256))
        .build();
    index.tokenizers().register("fs_default", analyzer);
}
```

### 3. N-gram Generation (CASS pattern with XF optimizations)
```rust
fn generate_edge_ngrams(text: &str) -> String {
    let mut ngrams = String::with_capacity(text.len() * 2);
    for word in text.split(|c: char| !c.is_alphanumeric()) {
        let indices: ArrayVec<usize, 17> = word
            .char_indices()
            .map(|(i, _)| i)
            .chain(std::iter::once(word.len()))
            .take(17)
            .collect();
        
        if indices.len() < 3 { continue; }
        for &end_idx in &indices[2..] {
            if !ngrams.is_empty() { ngrams.push(' '); }
            ngrams.push_str(&word[..end_idx]);
        }
    }
    ngrams
}
```
- Min: 2 chars, Max: 16 chars (compromise of 15 and 20)
- ArrayVec: No heap allocation
- Max 16 indices (2-char + padding)

pub fn parse_lexical_query(raw: &str, index: &Index) -> Result<Box<dyn Query>> {
    // Step 1: Sanitize
    let sanitized = sanitize_query(raw)?;
    let query_text = sanitized.as_str().ok_or(anyhow!("empty query"))?;
    
    // Step 2: Try primary parse
    let parser = QueryParser::for_index(
        index,
        vec![subject_field, body_field], // Only full-text fields
    );
    
    match parser.parse_query(query_text) {
        Ok(q) => Ok(Box::new(apply_field_boost(q, subject_boost: 2.0, body_boost: 1.0))),
        Err(e) => {
            // Step 3: Fallback
            let terms = extract_terms(query_text);
            build_or_query(terms)
        }
    }
}

### 6. Schema Versioning (MCP pattern)
```rust
pub fn schema_hash() -> String {
    let (schema, _) = build_schema();
    let mut entries: Vec<String> = schema
        .fields()
        .map(|(f, e)| format!("{}:{:?}:{}", e.name(), e.field_type(), f.field_id()))
        .collect();
    entries.sort();
    
    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
    hasher.update(SCHEMA_VERSION.as_bytes());
    hasher.update(b"\n");
    for entry in &entries {
        hasher.update(entry.as_bytes());
        hasher.update(b"\n");
    }
    hex::encode(hasher.finalize())
}
```

### 7. Index Open/Create
```rust
pub fn open_or_create(path: &Path) -> Result<Self> {
    let schema = build_schema();
    let hash_path = path.join("schema_hash.json");
    let mut needs_rebuild = true;
    
    if hash_path.exists() {
        if let Ok(content) = std::fs::read_to_string(&hash_path) {
            if let Ok(json) = serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&content) {
                if json.get("schema_hash").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) == Some(&schema_hash()) {
                    needs_rebuild = false;
                }
            }
        }
    }
    
    if needs_rebuild {
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(path);
        std::fs::create_dir_all(path)?;
    }
    
    let index = if path.join("meta.json").exists() && !needs_rebuild {
        Index::open_in_dir(path)?
    } else {
        Index::create_in_dir(path, schema)?
    };
    
    register_tokenizer(&index);
    std::fs::write(&hash_path, format!(r#"{{"schema_hash":"{}"}}"#, schema_hash()))?;
    
    let writer = index.writer(50_000_000)?;
    Ok(TantivyIndex { index, writer })
}
```

### 8. Segment Management (CASS pattern)
```rust
pub fn optimize_if_idle(&mut self) -> Result<bool> {
    let segment_count = self.index.searchable_segment_ids()?.len();
    
    // Check threshold
    if segment_count < 4 { return Ok(false); }
    
    // Check cooldown
    let now_ms = SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)?.as_millis() as i64;
    let last_merge = LAST_MERGE_TS.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
    if last_merge > 0 && (now_ms - last_merge) < 300_000 {
        return Ok(false);
    }
    
    let segment_ids = self.index.searchable_segment_ids()?;
    let _ = self.writer.merge(&segment_ids); // Async
    LAST_MERGE_TS.store(now_ms, Ordering::Relaxed);
    Ok(true)
}

## SUMMARY: KEY DECISIONS FOR FRANKENSEARCH

| Decision | Rationale |
|----------|-----------|
| **Use explicit tokenizer registration** | Ensures 256-byte limit + consistent lowercasing across all operations |
| **ArrayVec for n-gram indices** | Zero allocation overhead; critical for millions of indexed documents |
| **16-char max n-gram length** | Balances recall (longer prefixes) vs. memory (CASS's 20 is excessive) |
| **Query-time field boost (2.0x subject)** | MCP pattern avoids index-time scoring; runtime flexibility |
| **SHA256 schema hash** | Deterministic rebuild trigger; survives binary updates |
| **Phrase detection + dual-field parsing** | XF pattern: exclude Basic-indexed prefix field from phrase queries |
| **Sanitization before parsing** | MCP pattern: consistent fallback behavior |
| **Async merge with 5-min cooldown** | CASS pattern: prevents latency spikes from segment merges |
| **Microsecond timestamps** | MCP pattern: future-proof, matches RRF fusion granularity |
| **Snippet + separate highlight ranges** | Hybrid: Tantivy for snippet context, custom byte offsets for rich highlighting |
| **String type for exact-match filters** | Prevents tokenization of IDs/slugs (e.g., agent names, document kinds) |

## Current Architecture Map

- `src/main.rs`: process entrypoint. It loads dotenv configuration, detects robot output mode, applies resource defaults, chooses the asupersync runtime flavor, parses CLI args, and delegates to `coding_agent_search::run_with_parsed`.

- `src/connectors/` plus `franken_agent_detection`: provider-specific session discovery and normalization into conversation/message models.
- `src/indexer/`: scan, salvage, canonical storage writes, lexical publish/rebuild, semantic backfill, and progress/health instrumentation. This is high-risk and currently dirty, so this loop avoids it.
- `src/storage/`: frankensqlite-backed source of truth with legacy rusqlite debt. This is high-risk and currently dirty, so this loop avoids it.
- `src/search/`: query parsing, lexical/hybrid/semantic search, model management, daemon client, and robot metadata. Changes here require focused tests and schema caution.
- `src/pages/`, `src/html_export/`: export, encryption, bundle, preview, deployment, profiles, and browser-facing static assets. Good source of bounded helpers and private trait boilerplate.
- `src/analytics/`: usage rollups, query/reporting surfaces, validation, and UI chart data. Good source of local projection or repeated validation simplifications when tests are available.
- `src/ui/`: TUI state, rendering, data cache, charts, theme, and component helpers. High volume, but private formatting/fixture helpers can be safe when well-tested.
- `tests/`: integration and golden contracts. Good for DRYing repeated fixture code only if test names/assertions stay unchanged.

# Fifth Loop Architecture Notes

## Purpose

`cass` is a Rust 2024 CLI/TUI that indexes local and remote coding-agent
conversation histories, normalizes them into a shared model, persists them to
SQLite via frankensqlite, and serves human/TUI plus robot JSON search surfaces.

## Main Layers

- Entry/runtime: `src/main.rs` handles fatal-error formatting, robot-mode error
  envelopes, AVX/runtime setup, and delegates parsed commands into `src/lib.rs`.
- CLI contract: `src/lib.rs` defines clap commands, aliases, robot docs,
  structured error kinds, command execution, health/status/doctor surfaces,
  search/export/timeline/sources/models/pages/analytics dispatch, and many
  CLI contract tests.
- Connectors: `src/connectors/*` wraps `franken_agent_detection` and per-agent
  adapters that emit normalized conversations/messages/snippets.
- Storage: `src/storage/sqlite.rs` is the durable archive layer. Per repo rules,
  new SQLite work must use frankensqlite/compat APIs rather than new rusqlite.
- Indexing: `src/indexer/*` scans connectors, writes canonical storage,
  updates semantic data, and rebuilds/publishes lexical assets with atomic
  swap/backup semantics.
- Search: `src/search/*` owns lexical/vector/semantic readiness, policy,
  query execution, model management, reranking, and daemon client integration.
- Presentation: `src/ui/*` implements the FrankenTUI app; `src/pages/*` and
  `src/pages_assets/*` generate browser/export pages; `src/html_export/*`
  renders self-contained encrypted or plain HTML session exports.
- Operations: `src/sources/*` handles remote source setup/probing/sync and path
  mappings; `src/analytics/*` computes dashboard/bucketing/reporting data.

## Data Flow

```
CLI/TUI command
  -> command dispatch in src/lib.rs
  -> connector discovery / source sync / session scan
  -> normalized Conversation/Message/Snippet model
  -> frankensqlite archive as source of truth
  -> derived lexical/vector/semantic search assets
  -> robot JSON, TUI views, exports, pages, analytics
```

## Refactor Safety Boundaries

- Public robot JSON, error envelopes, exit-code kind strings, and golden docs
  are stable user contracts.
- Search indexes are derived assets; refactors must not add deletion-oriented
  repair flows or manual index removal recipes.
- Connector parsing preserves source provenance, timestamps, roles, and tool
  flattening semantics.
- HTML export and key-management changes need byte/string contract tests
  because files are portable artifacts.
- Any simplification crossing async, I/O, database, or search-ranking boundaries
  is high risk and should be avoided in this loop unless thoroughly pinned.
